investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received the orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence required by the expected-output contract.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending state until the eval timeout fires. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this infrastructure condition; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: existing remote-agent pods or other workloads consuming the peerpods VM slots have not been released, leaving zero allocatable capacity for new pods.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes may have lost the label or taint required by the remote-agent pod spec, reducing the schedulable pool from a larger set to only 2 nodes and making quota exhaustion more likely.

Tertiary — cluster under-provisioning: the total kata.peerpods.io/vm quota across the 2 eligible nodes may be too small for the concurrent eval workload, causing transient exhaustion even without a leak.

Quaternary — stuck or leaked remote-agent pods from a prior eval run holding VM slots without releasing them, preventing new pods from being scheduled (the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to prevent this, but a cleanup failure could leave orphaned pods).

investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in the production-api environment because every pod submitted for remote agent creation was rejected by the Kubernetes scheduler with an Unschedulable verdict: 2 nodes reported Insufficient kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity and 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because no pod was ever scheduled, no VM was provisioned, and the eval runner never received the orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, or remoteState evidence required by the expected-output contract.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the production-api remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource quota on the 2 nodes that carry that resource label. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. With 0 of 6 nodes schedulable and preemption unable to free capacity (no lower-priority victims found), every remote-agent pod is stuck in Pending state until the eval timeout fires. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling constraint, not an application code defect. The eval failure is a direct and accurate reflection of this infrastructure condition; no evidence of a user-traffic or production incident signal is present in the packet.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If a re-fetch of https://cypher-asi.github.io/aura-os/observability/status.json returns a snapshotAgeMinutes value <= 300, the snapshot has since been refreshed and the workflow is now healthy — disproving an ongoing pipeline failure.

If GitHub Actions workflow run history shows successful runs within the past 300 minutes with no failures, the staleness would need to be explained by a Pages CDN caching delay rather than a workflow execution gap.

If the snapshotAgeMinutes computation in statusSnapshotEvidence() (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs) is shown to have a clock or timezone bug that inflates the computed age, the actual artifact may be fresher than 717 minutes — disproving the staleness diagnosis.

If the published snapshot's embedded generatedAt timestamp, when parsed independently, shows a time within 300 minutes of the eval run at 2026-08-08T00:39:09Z, the age computation in the runner would be the defect rather than the workflow publishing cadence.

If all sibling checks had also failed (e.g., public-observability-page returning non-200), a broader infrastructure outage would be a more plausible cause — but all three siblings passed, making this scenario already disproved by the current evidence.
